svg.text: K9c DESIGN-TO-COST — K9b SCHLICHT built from cheaper parts
K9b's machine rebuilt from a printer gantry, a Gastro table, a €50 induction plate, a donor dishwasher.
6 actuators · 2 dynamic seals · ≈ 28 custom part types
est. coverage ≈ 94 % (233 of 248 meals, as K9b)
FRONT VIEW (fronts and glazed panels removed)
transport gallery z 2000–2200, ceiling ports into each module
TOP VIEW (cell at deck level z 870)
chute + blade post → bio bin 20 L
hub: T + S motors, coil fed by a €50 plate
THE HAND — printer/CNC-class Cartesian gantry at the rear wall (as K9b, cheaper parts)
X: open-loop NEMA 23, HTD 3M-15 belt, 2 × MGN15 rails on a 40 × 80 profile; labyrinth, no seal
Z: SFU1610 ball screw + brake motor on the hanging mast (band 1) · Y: NEMA 17 + belt in the arm tube (band 2)
roll: NEMA 23 + 20:1 planetary, canned magnet coupling · arm-root load cell weighs and senses collisions
Klipper on an Octopus Pro + Raspberry Pi 5 · 1 camera · push 300 N (y ≤ 420) / 150 N at full reach · 0.8 m/s
3 Diced in the press cup on the hub
4 Cooked + stirred on the heated hub
6 Hook rod: tray into the oven
printer gantry instead of industrial modules
hobby motors, coil fed by a €50 plate

g.text: 1/9 Box lowered through the ceiling port to the box shelf; the hand spears a potato
2/9 Potato rolled against the blade post over the chute: the peel falls into the bio bin
3/9 Into the press cup on the hub: T turns the screw base, the potato is pushed through the dicer grid
4/9 Hub heats: its ring coil runs on the generator board of a bought €50 induction plate; S stirs
5/9 Frikadellen fried on the domino front zone; the hand turns the pan pair (roll 180°)
6/9 Hook rod opens the oven above the well; GN tray of potatoes goes in
7/9 Plating into the hatch drawer; the diner pulls the drawer out at the front
8/9 Dish turned over the chute: scraps into the bio bin
9/9 Ware on edge into the well — the donor dishwasher's own tub, cut open at the top; its door stays shut
